transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-10-07 15:00 PDT | Duration: 55 minutes | Recording: Fireflies
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Liu (Redwood SE), Nadia Ortiz (Sunfire, Head MLOps), Rahul Mehta (Sunfire, Security Architect), Tom Becker (Sunfire, PM)

[00:00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. quick agenda, security gating items — sso, audit logs, retention, soc two docs — then a short results / tuning check and wrap with next steps.
[00:00:18] Tom Becker: sounds good. we have about an hour so that should fit.

--- Security/Compliance items ---
[00:01:05] Rahul Mehta: first off, thanks. big thing for us is SSO. we need a SAML flow that maps to our groups for RBAC. can you confirm what claims Redwood expects and whether we can map groups to roles?
[00:01:37] Marcus Liu: yep, so our hosted platform supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC, and we expose group claims in the SAML assertion. normally we map the groups to roles at the tenant level — you can configure RBAC rules in the console. we'll send the exact attribute names in the packet.
[00:02:05] Nadia Ortiz: is there anything special for service accounts? we rotate service keys quarterly, and need automated rotation support.
[00:02:22] Lena Park: good question. we have short-lived tokens for service accounts and support automatic key rotation with KMS integration. Marcus, do you want to add the details?
[00:02:30] Marcus Liu: sure — we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS / Azure KeyVault / GCP KMS) for envelope encryption. service tokens are minted with a one-hour TTL by default, but you can extend that via a policy for internal tooling. rotation can be automated via the management API.
[00:03:10] Rahul Mehta: any HSM options? we prefer HSM-backed keys for the production pilot.
[00:03:20] Marcus Liu: yes, if you bring your own HSM we can plug that in for on-prem or private deployments; for hosted we support KMS keys with customer-managed keys; full HSM integration is an option for dedicated/private installs.

[00:04:00] Tom Becker: audit logs — how verbose are they? we need to ship to our SIEM and retain for 365 days per policy.
[00:04:12] Marcus Liu: logs include request metadata, model used, token counts, latency, and user identity (where available). we can export as JSON or syslog, and you can forward via a connector to Splunk/Datadog/SIEM. retention on hosted is configurable, default 90 days; for Dedicated or Private we can match your 365-day retention.
[00:04:48] Nadia Ortiz: can we get a sample export so our SIEM team can validate parsing?
[00:04:55] Marcus Liu: yes — i'll prepare a synthetic export and a small ingestion script. expect json lines with fields like request_id, user_id, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, region, outcome, error_code. note: sometimes "kv cache" transcribed as K V cash in old logs but the field name is kv_cache_hit boolean.
[00:05:28] Rahul Mehta: good to know. and for PII, do you redaction pre or post logging?
[00:05:40] Marcus Liu: by default we log metadata only, not full prompt contents. for the pilot we can enable prompt capture with redaction — we have built-in PII scrubbing that can run prior to storage. alternatively, you can opt to never store prompt text.

--- Results review & tuning ---
[00:06:30] Lena Park: quick update on the metrics we collected this week — Nadia you saw the dashboard — average 95th percentile latency was 160ms for the short chat workload and p99 around 410ms during peak. cost per 1k tokens is roughly $0.90 using the small alpaca-variant quantized run; dedicated config lowered cost by about 22%.
[00:07:03] Nadia Ortiz: yes that matches our telemetry. we saw a few spikes in the afternoon when batch sizes grew. any tuning tips?
[00:07:14] Marcus Liu: a couple things: reduce max batch size for latency-sensitive routes, enable prefix/KV caching for repeated context across sessions, and consider int8 quantization profile for your heavier rerank step — that reduced memory by ~30% in our bench. also evaluate batching windows — we had one misconfig where batching waited 200ms, pushing some requests up to p99.
[00:07:48] Tom Becker: i remember the model fallback behavior — if load gets high do you automatically route to a cheaper model?
[00:07:56] Lena Park: yes we have smart routing policies: route by latency SLA or cost. for the pilot you can enable canary fallback to a smaller model when latency thresholds breach. we can show the routing policy config in the console.

--- Specific security Q&A ---
[00:09:10] Rahul Mehta: SOC2 — are you certified? we need a copy of the report and an attestation for our procurement.
[00:09:20] Lena Park: Redwood is SOC2 Type II audited; i'll send the report and AICPA letter. Marcus, we'll add the version info for the underlying infra.
[00:09:33] Marcus Liu: noted. we'll include infrastructure segmentation diagrams, control mapping, and service boundaries.
[00:09:45] Nadia Ortiz: DPIA/GDPR — what controls for EU data residency?
[00:09:55] Marcus Liu: we can pin processing to specific regions and we offer Private deployments for strict residency. for hosted we support region selection and data residency options; for regulated data we recommend Private.

[00:11:02] Tom Becker: any known limitations about VPC peering? our networking team is strict about inbound rules.
[00:11:12] Marcus Liu: we do VPC peering and private endpoints; typically we provide a set of egress IPs and peer subnets. we'll do a network whiteboard with your infra team.

--- Live SSO test walkthrough (discussion) ---
[00:13:00] Lena Park: Nadia, you mentioned earlier you wanted to test SSO on the staging tenant. is that still the case?
[00:13:07] Nadia Ortiz: yes — we'll test tomorrow in our window. we need the metadata and a staging certificate.
[00:13:15] Marcus Liu: i'll upload SAML metadata and send the cert in the follow-up. note that group mapping will require an attribute called "redwood_groups" — we'll include that in the packet.
[00:13:40] Rahul Mehta: also can we get logs of the auth flow for debugging?
[00:13:46] Marcus Liu: yes, auth audit logs can be included in the export sample. they show assertion time, subject, attributes, and auth outcome.

--- Concerns and clarifications ---
[00:15:20] Nadia Ortiz: i have a question about prompt retention during a bug reproduce — if we need to capture prompt text for debugging, what's the process and how do you ensure it's purged?
[00:15:34] Marcus Liu: we have an on-demand secure capture mode. captured prompts are stored encrypted, retention policy can be set per-tenant, and deletions are enforced through the control plane with verifiable deletion logs. we'll provide docs on retention APIs.

[00:16:10] Tom Becker: any caveats on private deployment lead times? our timeline for go/no-go is end of month.
[00:16:22] Lena Park: Private deployments take longer — typically 6–8 weeks for on-prem or full private stack. Dedicated with customer-managed keys is faster, 2–3 weeks, if the networking is pre-approved. for the pilot we'll stay hosted with private tenant controls.

--- Short demo references/links ---
[00:18:00] Lena Park: i'll drop links after the call: SSO setup doc, audit-log schema, SOC2 packet, and the console screenshots for routing policy.

--- Closing recap and next steps ---
[00:18:50] Lena Park: recap: we will send SOC2 plus architecture, Marcus will send the audit-log sample and ingestion script, Rahul will share SIEM schema, Nadia will run SSO test. we'll schedule network whiteboard for VPC peering next week.
[00:19:10] Rahul Mehta: sounds good. if we can validate the audit export and SSO by the 14th we can move to the compliance gate decision.
[00:19:22] Nadia Ortiz: agreed. do we need to extend the pilot if anything pops up?
[00:19:28] Lena Park: yes we can extend one additional two-week pilot if necessary — just notify the AE.

[00:20:00] Marcus Liu: small note — we found one edge case in the reranker where long context makes kv cache thrash, we recommended document-level chunking to avoid re-computing big KV windows. we'll provide a quick config sample.

[00:21:12] Tom Becker: okay that's useful. anything else from Sunfire side?
[00:21:20] Nadia Ortiz: no, thanks.
[00:21:23] Rahul Mehta: nothing else.

[00:21:30] Lena Park: great — thanks everyone. i'll send the follow-ups and we will reconvene after the SSO test.
[00:21:38] Tom Becker: thanks all.

(Recording continues with small side chatter and some crosstalk; final 30 minutes were Q/A and scheduling; transcript here is truncated to the key segments for the security review and pilot tuning.)
